# Pixel 10a: Everything you need, at a price you’ll love

Feb 18, 2026

 The new Pixel 10a packs core Pixel experiences into a sleek, durable design for just $499. 

Laura Kastilani

Product Manager

Our Pixel A-series phones always offer our most helpful features at an accessible price point. And with the new Pixel 10a, we’re making many of our advanced AI tools and best-in-class camera system available for just $499.

## Smooth by design

Pixel 10a’s refined smooth design features a completely flat back. The camera bar blends seamlessly with the back of the phone, so it easily slips in and out of your pocket, and lies perfectly flat wherever you place it.

Designed with sustainability in mind, Pixel 10a is made with the most recycled material of any A-series Pixel yet, including for the first time recycled cobalt, copper, gold and tungsten. 1 It has a satin-finish 100% recycled aluminium frame and an 81% recycled plastic back cover. 2 

 

Pixel 10a debuts a reimagined color story, blending a sophisticated palette with a bold new energy for the season. It comes in Lavender, Berry, Fog and Obsidian.

## Built to last, and with even more battery life

Pixel 10a is our most durable A-series phone yet thanks to IP68 water and dust protection and durable materials. 3 With an upgraded Corning® Gorilla® Glass 7i cover glass on the display it’s exceptionally designed to deliver improved durability for better scratch and drop resistance. 4 The 6.3-inch Actua display is also 11% brighter than Pixel 9a, so your photos and videos look vibrant even in direct sunlight.

It also has faster charging than Pixel 9a, with more than 30 hours of battery life and up to 120 with Extreme Battery Saver turned on. 5 Plus, Pixel 10a will come with seven years of OS, security and Pixel Drops. 6 And for added peace of mind, we’re bringing Satellite SOS to the A-series for the first time, so you can connect with emergency services even when you’re without Wi-Fi or cellular service. 7 

 

## A camera for extraordinary photos every day

Pixel 10a has the best camera under $500 with a 48MP main camera and a 13MP ultrawide camera. In fact, our A-series phones have had the best-in-class camera five generations in a row. 8 Capture crisp details up close with Macro Focus and in low light with Night Sight.

It also features some of our most popular photo tools, available to the A-series for the first time:

- Auto Best Take helps make sure everyone in a group photo looks their best with a single shutter press. Pixel automatically analyzes multiple frames to find the perfect shot.
- Camera Coach uses Gemini models to give you step-by-step guidance on lighting and composition, helping you take better pictures and become a better photographer. 9 

Plus, you can use Google Photos to edit just by asking with the help of AI, either by typing in the changes you want or speaking them directly to your phone. 10 And now Add Me can support small and large group pics — so squeeze your cousins, aunts, uncles and great-grandparents (and even your dog) into the family reunion pic, then add yourself to it!

And when you're ready to share your photos and important moments, the kind of device you have doesn't matter now that Quick Share works with AirDrop®. 11 

 

 

 

 

 

 

## Powered by Google Tensor, with AI features and Gemini

Pixel 10a is powered by our custom-built Google Tensor G4 chip, giving you total access to Gemini — your personal AI assistant. You can do things like use Gemini Live to have natural, back-and-forth conversations. 12 Or play with Nano Banana to reimagine your photos, blend images together or apply different creative styles to make them your own. 13 

You can also use other AI-powered features like Circle to Search to learn more about anything on your screen by simply circling, tapping or highlighting it. 14 And Dialer features like Call Screen and Hold For Me save you time and help you avoid spammers.

## Pre-order Pixel 10a today

Pixel 10a is available for $499 starting March 5 at the Google Store and major carriers. Phone cases will be available in Lavender, Berry, Fog and Obsidian, and so you can match your case to your phone, or mix it up with fun color combinations. Plus, we’re launching Pixel Buds 2a in two new colors, Berry and Fog, to complement Pixel 10a.

# Galaxy A54 Camera in 2026: Reviewer Findings and Settings

What reviewers found about the Galaxy A54 camera, the settings that suit it, One UI 9 as its last major update, and how it compares with the A55 to A57.

By Samsung Photography Academy Editorial Team· May 15, 2026· Updated November 6, 2026

↑ Part of the Galaxy Phones hub Best Samsung Phone for Photography in 2026: Every Galaxy Camera Ranked

The Samsung Galaxy A54 debuted with a 50MP OIS camera in March 2023 for $449 (US). Since then, Samsung has released three more Galaxy A5x series phones, the latest being the Galaxy A57 (March 2026). Chances are if you’re shopping for a Galaxy A54 today, you’ll find yourself looking at either old stock or second-hand options.

The good news is that the Samsung Galaxy A54’s 50MP OIS camera still manages to deliver. The less exciting news is that as we move further into 2026, the more pertinent question becomes how much longer Samsung will continue to support the Galaxy A54 with software updates.

Pictures taken during the day with the Galaxy A54’s 50MP main camera (with OIS) are sharp and have natural colours. GSMArena also rated the phone’s low-light shots highly. The Galaxy A54’s ultrawide and 5MP macro cameras are less impressive. The Galaxy A54 will get One UI 9 (Android 17) as its fourth and final major OS upgrade and is promised security patches for five years from its launch date. Consider buying the Galaxy A54 only at a clear discount.

## Galaxy A54 camera specs

| Camera | Hardware | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main | 50MP, f/1.8, 23mm, 1/1.56-inch sensor, OIS | Saves 12.5MP binned photos by default, with a 50MP mode |
| Ultrawide | 12MP, f/2.2, 13mm, 123° | Fixed focus |
| Macro | 5MP, f/2.4 | Fixed focus at about 4cm |
| Front | 32MP, f/2.2, 26mm | Saves 12MP in the wide view and 8MP in the cropped view |
| Video | 4K30 on the main and ultrawide cameras, 1080p60 on the main | 4K stabilisation arrived in a software update |
| Chip and software | Exynos 1380, launched on Android 13 | Updating to One UI 9 (Android 17) |

Specs from GSMArena's A54 spec sheet and review.

## How the A54 camera performs

We don’t have an A54 to hand so can’t comment on image quality ourselves, but according to GSMArena’s review, daylight shots from the main camera are excellent, with accurate white balance, wide dynamic range and unobtrusive sharpening. Switching to 50MP adds a little detail but isn’t magic – grass, for example, still isn’t going to resolve all that well.

According to GSMArena’s review, the main camera also performs well at night. It’s worth noting that Photo mode will engage some sort of night-time processing when conditions warrant, so Night mode often won’t offer much in the way of additional benefit (at least on the 1x camera; the ultrawide produces rather washed-out colours in poor light, and GSMArena reckons Night mode only improves things a little).

There’s no telephoto camera, so tapping 2x in the camera app performs a crop from the 50MP main camera – GSMArena’s review suggests these aren’t bad at all – and anything beyond that is digital zoom. The 5MP macro camera has a fixed focus distance of around 4cm, so be prepared to get up close and personal (and watch out for casting your phone’s shadow onto your subject!). There are a couple of workarounds in the macro photography guide.

Video capture maxes out at 4K30. Stabilisation was limited to 1080p video at launch, but GSMArena has since updated its review to reflect the fact that Samsung has added stabilisation for 4K footage via a software update. Footage shot in poor lighting conditions is GSMArena’s least favourite, however, with colours looking a little washed out and highlights a touch harsh.

## Settings that suit the A54

| Situation | What to use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Everyday daylight | 1x main camera at the default resolution | Clean files and the fastest shooting |
| Static scene you'll crop | 50MP mode in bright light | More definition when you have light to spare |
| Evening and night | Photo mode on the 1x camera, phone braced | Night processing already runs in dim scenes |
| Portraits | Portrait mode at 1x or 2x, blur turned down | GSMArena found the default blur a little strong |
| Moving subjects | Pro mode on the main camera with a fast shutter | Pro mode is available on the main camera |
| Close-ups | Macro mode at about 4cm, in good light | The macro lens can't focus any closer or further |
| Video | 4K30 or 1080p60 on the main camera | The ultrawide struggles in low light |

Pro mode gives you even more options and lets you choose settings like shutter speed and ISO. The Pro mode guide explains the order to set them in. For dim scenes, the Night mode guide covers situations when it makes sense to use the dedicated mode.

## A54 vs A55, A56 and A57

| | Galaxy A54 | Galaxy A55 | Galaxy A56 | Galaxy A57 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Announced | March 2023 | March 2024 | March 2025 | March 2026 |
| Main camera | 50MP, f/1.8, OIS, 1/1.56-inch | 50MP, f/1.8, OIS, 1/1.56-inch | 50MP, f/1.8, OIS, 1/1.56-inch | 50MP, f/1.8, OIS, 1/1.56-inch |
| Ultrawide | 12MP, f/2.2 | 12MP, f/2.2 | 12MP, f/2.2 | 12MP, f/2.2 |
| Macro | 5MP | 5MP | 5MP | 5MP |
| Front camera | 32MP | 32MP | 12MP | 12MP |
| Chip | Exynos 1380 | Exynos 1480 | Exynos 1580 | Exynos 1680 |
| Frame | Plastic | Aluminium | Aluminium | Aluminium |
| Major OS updates promised | 4 | 4 | 6 | 6 |

Specs from GSMArena's spec sheets for each phone.

Image processing and speeds set the four phones apart, as the main cameras are identical on paper (there’s no telephoto lens on any of the models). All four feature a 50MP f/1.8 main camera with OIS. According to GSMArena, the A57’s camera hardware is identical to that of the A56; it’s the image processing and camera speeds that have been tweaked. Selfie camera specs and lengths of software support also vary. The Galaxy A56 camera guide and the Galaxy A55 camera guide go through those phones in detail. The Galaxy A55 settings page has a list of initial values for the newer phone.

None of these phones has a telephoto. If zoom matters, the Galaxy S26 FE adds an 8MP 3x telephoto. Our guide to the A57 and A37 covers Samsung's current mid-range pair.

## Software updates and Galaxy AI

Samsung promised four generations of Android updates and five years of security updates for the Galaxy A54 at the time of its launch. One UI 9 with Android 17 has started rolling out in South Korea as per a report by SamMobile and has since expanded to India and other countries/regions as of early November 2026. Since this is the fourth update for the phone, you shouldn’t expect any more Android updates. However, security updates should continue till around 2028.

One UI 8 also added some Galaxy AI-based photo editing features to the Galaxy A54 5G. According to Samsung’s Canadian support page, the Galaxy A54 5G gets One UI 8’s Generative photo editing feature that can remove/move objects in images using the Gallery app. This feature will require a Samsung account, and images edited with it will have an AI watermark. The Galaxy A54 already had Object Eraser and Remaster features when it launched (via SamMobile).

## Should you buy a Galaxy A54 in 2026?

If you can pick one up at a steep discount off the price of an A56, and you tend to take most of your pictures in daytime or at-home scenarios, it’s worth buying, as the A54’s camera is still pretty good. It also retains 2x cropping and Pro mode, both of which are carried over to newer models.

But if you want a handset that’ll stick around for four or five more years, you’ll want to look elsewhere, as the A54 has no major Android updates left, and will see an even shorter stretch of security-only support.

Upgrading from the A54? There’s not much of a camera-related reason to move up to the A55. You’re better off getting an A56 or A57, which come with a speedier chip and two additional promised generations of OS updates, or jumping to Samsung’s FE models in the S-series line for a dedicated telephoto camera.

### Checks before buying a used A54

- Visit Settings > Software update and see if One UI 9 is available for download or already installed. If your Galaxy phone is lagging far behind, it could be down to a slow rollout from your carrier (if it’s a carrier model).
- Hold the phone up to a bright light and check the glass covering your rear cameras for any scratches. A scratched camera lens can result in blurry and light-flared photos, and there’s no camera setting that can compensate for this.
- Focus check: Use each of your Galaxy phone’s cameras (including 2x and Macro) to take a few test snaps. The primary camera should snap focus when pointed at objects up close.
- Shake check: To make sure video stabilisation is still going strong, record a brief video while taking a few steps.

Should I buy the A54 or the A55 in 2026?+

Get the A55 if the price difference isn’t that much, as it’s a better phone all round (aluminium frame, faster chip, longer-lasting updates) and has the same main camera as the A54 anyway. If the A54 is significantly cheaper though, then get that.

Does the A54 still get updates?+

It does for now. One UI 9 (Android 17) began rolling out in late 2026 as the device’s fourth and final promised OS update, and it will receive security updates until around 2028 under Samsung’s five-year security support pledge.

Is the A54 camera good for photography beginners?+

It's a good starter camera with OIS (optical image stabilisation) for its main camera that can result in steadier photos taken in-hand. Its Pro mode is also good for learning about manual camera controls like shutter speed and ISO for exposure control. Where the camera falls short is zoom and low-light performance for its ultrawide camera.

Samsung Photography Academy has 60+ short 5-minute lessons that teach you how to get the most out of your Samsung Galaxy camera, whichever model it is (even the A series is covered), including which camera to use, and the different modes you can use. It comes with a 60-day money-back guarantee.

# Google Pixel 10A review – still a great camera phone for budget buyers

: out of 5

 

 Joshua Waller 

2 October 2026 / 15:19 BST 2 October 2026 / 15:19 BST

Google Pixel 10A in grey. Photo JW/AP

## The Google Pixel 10A may seem almost identical to last years model, but that doesn't stop it being a great camera phone for budget buyers. 

Amateur Photographer verdict

The Google Pixel 10A is a good value option with a great set of features, but Google’s own phones offer strong competition – especially the 9A which is cheaper.

Pros

- Good overall camera setup for the price
- Easy to use AI features
- Nice photo results

Cons

- Little change since the last phone
- Minimal pro/manual controls
- 128GB storage is looking low

The Google Pixel 10A was introduced as the budget model in Google’s 2026 range of phones, and at an RRP of $499 (128GB) is up against a range of competitors from Samsung (with the triple camera A57 at £529 / 256GB), and Apple (with the single camera 17e at £599 with 256GB) it feels like Google have got some stiff competition, already at a disadvantage with only 128GB storage. Does it justify a place among our best budget phones? Find out…

Google Pixel 10A in grey. Photo JW/AP

### At a glance: 

- 48MP wide-angle camera, f/1.7, 25mm, PDAF, OIS, 4K 60p 
- 13MP ultra-wide, f/2.2, 14mm equivalent, (120°), 4K 30p 
- 13MP selfie camera, f/2.2, 20mm equivalent, 4K 30p, fixed focus 
- 6.3inch FullHD P-OLED, 120Hz screen, 3000nits peak brightness 
- Battery: 5100mAh (30W charging, 10W wireless) 
- 7 years of OS/Security/Feature updates 

### How we test phones

We review phones from the perspective of choosing one for its photography and camera performance, so here we look at what the Google Pixel 8A offers in terms of its cameras and the features included for photography and video. 

Google Pixel 10A in grey – the bump has gone entirely. Photo JW/AP

### Hardware, Design and Features 

The cameras on the 10A remain the same as the cameras on the 9A, with a 48MP wide-angle main camera, with f/1.7 aperture, 25mm equivalent and phase detection autofocus (PDAF) as well as optical image stabilisation (OIS) – this camera gives 12MP pixel-binned images. There’s a 13MP ultra-wide camera, with f/2.2 aperture giving a 14mm equivalent (120°), and it is fixed focus. Finally, there’s a 13MP selfie camera with f/2.2 aperture, and 20mm equivalent, again it’s fixed focus. There is no telephoto camera, but a 2x option is available on the phone, with zoom going up to 8x.

The main camera offers impressive close-up focus, for a standard 1x camera, and a macro icon will appear on screen when it detects the subject is close enough. Unlike some phones, it doesn’t us the ultra-wide for macro, and as there is no telephoto camera, it can’t use that either, so it’s nice to see the main camera with close-focus, as this allows for a less distorted view compared to an ultra-wide. 

4K 60p is available from the main camera, 4K 30p from the other cameras, including the selfie camera. 

The screen benefits from a fast refresh rate, up to 120Hz, and a peak brightness of 3000nits. The borders look large if you’re used to flagship phones, but larger boarders are common on entry-level phones. You also get a reasonably large battery (at 5100mAh), and the phone supports wireless charging. The phone’s IP67 rated, so it’ll withstand an accidental soaking here and there. 

Google Pixel 10A in grey. Photo JW/AP

The ultra-wide-angle camera is fixed focus, with a 14mm equivalent (0.5x on screen setting), and has an f/2.2 aperture, which is fairly standard. As the camera doesn’t have auto-focus, you won’t be able to use this for macro photography, but luckily the main camera has decent close focus performance. 

Google Pixel 10A in grey. Space Odyssey 2001 anyone? Photo JW/AP

### Google PIXEL 10A vs 9A:

The Pixel 10A offers very slight changes in size and weight, now slightly thicker, but of note is an improved charging speed for both wired and wireless, which are now 30W and 10W respectively.

There are no changes in the cameras, or processor between the 9A and 10A. Battery life remains the same with a 5100mAh rated battery. Impressive for a ‘budget’ phone, beating even some premium phones from other brands. 

Google Pixel 9A in white (left), 10A in grey. Photo JW/AP

The Pixel 10A has a 9mm thick body, slightly thicker than the 9A (at 8.9mm). This makes the phone seem thicker than most phones, at nearly 1cm thick. The camera “bump” – what was left of it on the 9A – is completely gone on the 10A.

Google Pixel 10A selfie camera. Photo JW/AP

The punch-hole selfie camera is a 13MP camera with an f/2.2 aperture and is also fixed focus. 

### The camera app 

There are a range of photo modes that will be of benefit to photographers, for example, there’s a long exposure mode that can be used for light trails or smooth flowing water and waterfalls. There’s a portrait mode with 1.7x and 2x options, as well. However, there are no manual modes available, something that looks particularly poor considering even Apple have now added manual controls. 

You get the ‘night sight’ photo mode, which gives you access to Google’s impressive night photography. This lets you shoot with Auto or even longer with the Max setting. If you place the phone on a solid surface or a tripod, then you can access the astrophotography mode, which lets you take a 4minute exposure (with a 5 second timer automatically switched on). There’s also a panoramic photo mode. 

Google Pixel 10A in photo mode. Photo JW/AP

Beyond this, you won’t find any specific scene modes, and in this area, there are more options and scene modes on other cameras, with only the Google Pixel Pro phones offering a manual mode. 

Even though there are no manual controls available on the photo app, you do get a variety of controls, including raw shooting, white balance, shadow adjustment and brightness. 

### “Camera Coach” AI Features 

This is an AI powered photo assistant that provides real-time guides on framing, lighting, and composition. You can use this if you want, or you can simply ignore it, depending on your preferences. I went for the latter option. 

Once you get into playback, you’ll find a range of Google’s AI editing tools and options. It’s currently fairly uncommon to see AI editing features outside of flagship Samsung and Apple phones. 

The ‘Best Take’ feature lets you change the subjects face from another photo, when you’ve taken multiple photos of people. If you haven’t, then the phone can struggle to give you enough choices. 

Google Pixel 10A in photo mode. Photo JW/AP

There is, of course, the usual built-in Magic eraser, Unblur, Portrait blur and Sky options found under Tools in the photo editor. The Magic eraser works well and makes it easy to remove unwanted objects from a photo. 

### Performance and Image Quality 

I’ve taken hundreds of photos with the Google Pixel 10A, taking it with me everywhere I went. Here are some of the best images I’ve taken that demonstrate the results of this camera phone.

Ultra-wide (0.5x) – Pixel 10A. Photo JW

Wide (1x) – Pixel 10A. Photo JW

Zoom (2x hybrid) – Pixel 10A. Photo JW

Zoom (hybrid) – Pixel 10A. Photo JW

Zoom (8x hybrid) – Pixel 10A. Photo JW

In bright sunny conditions, all cameras give great results, with pleasing colour that’s not too overly saturated. 

The ultra-wide-angle camera gives you an 0.5x view compared to the main (1x) camera. You’ve also got the option of a 2x zoom, which is an on-screen option. If you pinch to zoom, you can extend this to 8x, but detail drops off quickly (and images look like mush).

Pixel 10a · f/2.2 · 1/170s · 1.854mm · ISO52

Ultra-wide-angle photo taken in the trees. Photo Joshua Waller

The ultra-wide angle lens gives good results, but if you look at photos from this camera in detail, you can see some noise in images. When you compare these photos to photos from the main camera, you’ll quite quickly be able to see that results from the main camera are cleaner, with less noise visible.

Pixel 10a · f/1.7 · 1/1527s · 4.53mm · ISO26

Colour is nice. On the Edge, Park Hill flats, Sheffield. Photo Joshua Waller

With fairly pleasing colour reproduction, in sunny conditions, images look great. However, in poor weather you may find that images can look a little dull, but they’re simply a reflection of the shooting conditions, for example, in grey weather images can look very grey. 

Pixel 10a · f/2.2 · 1/40s · 1.854mm · ISO171

A book about cats. Photo Joshua Waller

In advanced options, you can switch on RAW/JPEG control to allow raw shooting, and Ultra HDR is switched on by default. This results in a high level of dynamic range being captured in photos, but for the most part, results look realistic rather than going over the top.

Pixel 10a · f/1.7 · 1/179s · 4.53mm · ISO23

Close-up of a cat using portrait mode. Portrait mode has blurred the background and the whiskers. Photo JW

The ultra-wide-angle camera doesn’t feature auto-focus, so can’t be used for close-ups or macro photography. 

Therefore, for close-up photography, you’re best bet is to use the main camera as the results are good, with a nice level of background blur, as well as reasonably close focus for some things.

Pixel 10a · f/1.7 · 1/33s · 4.53mm · ISO116

Low light mode. Lens flare is an issue in this image taken with the main camera. Photo JW

Shooting in low-light, the camera did a reasonable job, but saturation levels were duller than when shooting with a different camera phone (with a larger sensor), and with this photo we begin to see it struggle a little bit.

Pixel 10A selfie camera using portrait mode. Image JW

Pixel 10A selfie camera using photo mode. Image JW

When using the selfie camera, blur can be added to photos after you’ve taken the photo, or when shooting. This does a reasonable job at first glance, but if you look at the photo in detail, you can see where there are errors around the hair and some oddities in other areas of the image.

Pixel 10a · f/1.7 · 1/2653s · 4.53mm · ISO28

A detailed view of some shops. Photo JW

Video Recording 

Using the video mode, you can use zoom up to 5x, even when recording 4K video. You’re able to record 4K video from all cameras, including the ultra-wide, wide and the selfie camera. Colour, dynamic range and levels of detail are all good, although wind noise can be an issue, and quality suffers in low-light.

Google Pixel 9A in white (left), 10A in grey. Photo JW/AP

### Verdict 

If you’re looking for a phone with AI features, then the Google Pixel 10A is a good value option at its newly reduced price. However, for a larger screen, you’ll need to look beyond Google: the Samsung Galaxy A57 has such a screen and is currently about $450 / £355.

Pixel 10a · f/1.7 · 1/15625s · 4.53mm · ISO26

A nice view in the countryside. Photo Joshua Waller

There are lots of people out there that want a smaller phone, and very few companies still offer this, so it makes sense for Google to produce these options. The Pixel 10A is a great phone, but if you find the old Pixel 10 or 9 for a similar price, then go for it, as that has better hardware in the form of better cameras. 

Overall the phone takes some great photos in sunny conditions, and with additional AI features such as Add Me, Best Take, Magic Editor and Audio Magic Eraser, as well as 7 years of OS, security and feature updates, it makes for a good value package. 

Pixel 10a · f/2.2 · 1/148s · 1.854mm · ISO48

Nice colour reproduction comes as standard even using the ultra-wide. Photo JW
